messages:
sara: Quick follow-up to the retention/tagging RFC — need decisions on defaults and flow. My proposal: retention_class enum with values "billing_long" (7y), "audit_mid" (2y), "ephemeral" (30d). Also prefer storing tenant as a hashed identifier in raw events for PII reduction. Thoughts?

lee: +1 on hashed tenant_id. Reduces PII surface in raw stores. We should define the HMAC algorithm and salt rotation policy though.

 tom: hashed is fine but caution: backfills need deterministic hashes. If we rotate salt, previous hashes break. Suggest stable HMAC key per-tenant (rotate only on explicit migration).

nat: Legal chimed in — 7y for billing_long is acceptable for billing evidence, but some customers will ask for custom retention. Can we support per-tenant retention_override? Also need explicit "retention_class" in schema so ops can GC correctly.

sara: Yes — plan is: add retention_class enum + optional retention_override_ttl (seconds) on an account ACL. GC/compact jobs consult override first, fallback to class default.

lee: Operational question: audit pipeline sometimes needs raw payloads for disputes. If we GC raw events, how do we satisfy long-term evidence requests?

 tom: We should keep compacted aggregates + cryptographic receipts. Idea: for billing_long keep per-window aggregates (append-only) plus Merkle receipts per ingest batch. Receipts contain token counts + fingerprint, so we can prove an event existed without retaining raw PII.

nat: Merkle receipts sound good. Legal: receipts must be reproducible and include token counts, tenant_hash, and fingerprint. Also confirm they are retained at least as long as billing_long.

 sara: Draft payload example for discussion: ```{"event_id":"uuid","tenant_hash":"hmac:v1:...","retention_class":"billing_long","tokens":123,"fingerprint":"sha256:...","metadata":{"source":"api","model":"gptx"}}``` Any missing fields?

lee: Add a small "provenance" subfield: "provenance":{"ingest_version":"v1","received_at":"iso_ts"} — helps migrations and backfill logic.

 tom: For migration/backfill: if we change tenant hashing, add tenant_hash_v2 and keep tenant_hash_v1. Backfill will populate v2 over time; GC and queries will accept either until we cutover. Backfill command prototype: ```python backfill_tenant_hash.py --from 2024-01-01 --to 2025-01-01 --parallel=16```

nat: One more: billing windowing relies on event timestamps. When GC runs, we must keep aggregates forever (or as tenant dictates). So compaction must produce append-only ledger rows with signed proofs. Ops needs a migration plan for ledger schema to include signature fields.

 sara: Agreed — aggregates are canonical for billing and should be append-only with signature/verifier fields and retention matching billing_long by default. GC removes raw events but not aggregates/receipts.

metering-bot: deploy scheduled: retention-tagging-schema-v1 -> staging on 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC :rocket:

lee: Next steps: I'll draft the migration plan (schema change, backfill windows, key rotation policy).

 tom: I'll prototype the Merkle receipt generator and a verifier tool (CLI + small web lookup).

 nat: I'll confirm legal/reg retention ranges and update compliance checklist.

 sara: I'll update the RFC with the schema diff, ops checklist (GC job changes, compaction), and rollout plan. If no objections by EOD Friday we'll schedule the staged rollout. Thanks all :thumbsup:
